<div class="course-box">

## STAT 151A: Linear Modelling (Theory & Applications)

<div class="course-desc">
STAT 151A at UC Berkeley focuses on modern statistical inference and linear modeling, emphasizing both theoretical foundations and practical applications.
</div>

<style>
/* Ensuring the list styling is consistent across all course boxes */
.topic-text ul {
  margin: 0;
  padding-left: 25px !important; 
  list-style-type: disc !important;
  display: block !important;
}

.topic-text li {
  display: list-item !important;
  margin-bottom: 10px;
  line-height: 1.6;
  color: #003262;
  text-align: left;
}
</style>
```{=html}
<div class="topic-grid">
  <div class="topic-card">
    <div class="topic-label">Fundamentals</div>
    <div class="topic-text">
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Linear Algebra:</strong> Matrix formulation of the General Linear Model and OLS estimation.</li>
        <li><strong>Inference:</strong> Hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and the Gauss-Markov theorem.</li>
        <li><strong>Diagnostics:</strong> Model assessment, residual analysis, and identifying high-leverage points.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="topic-card">
    <div class="topic-label">Advanced Inference</div>
    <div class="topic-text">
      <ul>
        <li><strong>Regularization:</strong> Shrinkage methods including Ridge regression, LASSO, and Elastic Net.</li>
        <li><strong>Extensions:</strong> Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) for non-normal response variables.</li>
        <li><strong>Robustness:</strong> Outlier detection, influential observations, and robust regression techniques.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

<div class="course-desc">
Students learn to implement and interpret these models, assess assumptions, and address common pitfalls such as confounding, omitted variables, and high-leverage points.
</div>

<div class="note-box">
Solutions written by Ajay Sharma to <em>theoretical exercises</em> assigned throughout the semester. <em>Computational exercises</em> have <em>not</em> been shown.
</div>

## STAT 154/254: Modern Statistical Prediction & Machine Learning

<div class="course-desc">
STAT 154/254 at UC Berkeley covers a comprehensive set of foundational and advanced machine learning topics, blending statistical learning ideas with optimization and computation.
</div>

```{=html}
<div class="topic-grid">
  <div class="topic-card">
    <div class="topic-label" style="text-align:center; width:100%;">Basic Topics</div>
    <div class="topic-text" style="text-align:left; width:100%;">
      <ul style="margin:0; padding-left:20px;">
        <li><strong>Tasks:</strong> Regression, classification, dimension reduction, and clustering.</li>
        <li><strong>Algorithms:</strong> Solving linear systems, gradient descent, Newton’s method, power iteration for eigenvalue problems, and EM algorithms.</li>
        <li><strong>Others:</strong> Kernel methods, regularization, sample splitting, resampling methods, and cross-validation.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="topic-card">
    <div class="topic-label" style="text-align:center; width:100%;">Advanced Topics</div>
    <div class="topic-text" style="text-align:left; width:100%;">
      <ul style="margin:0; padding-left:20px;">
        <li>Statistical learning theory and optimization theory.</li>
        <li>Bagging and boosting, tree-based models, neural networks, and Bayesian models.</li>
        <li>Online learning and bandit problems.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```


<div class="course-desc">
The course emphasizes both mathematical understanding and algorithmic structure, with topics ranging from solving linear systems to modern predictive modeling.
</div>
